headline: Chromosome-level and draft genomes expand reference resources for non-model arthropods
label: Non Model Animal Genome Assemblies
summary: Recent releases add genomes for a pest gall wasp, four Culex West Nile virus vectors, and a soil ecotoxicology model mite.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the generation of genome references for non-model arthropods of applied interest. A chromosome-level 399 Mb assembly of the invasive wiliwili pest gall wasp Quadrastichus erythrinae is reported alongside its Wolbachia genome. The ERGA-BGE work provides chromosome-level reference genomes for four Mediterranean Culex species, key West Nile virus vectors, with contig and scaffold metrics. The Oppia nitens entry presents an annotated de novo hybrid draft (125.4 Mb, 65 scaffolds, N50 4.41 Mb, 99.1% BUSCO) for a standardized soil ecotoxicology model invertebrate. What is new is the extension of genome resources to these specific taxa. The mite assembly is a draft rather than chromosome-level, so its utility rests on completeness metrics rather than chromosomal architecture.
